system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: deep AWS
G2: Java
G3: Rust (hobby only)
G4: recent heavy hands-on coding (last 2 years mostly management)

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Keeping a director-level CV that screams over-qualified for an IC ad instead of foregrounding hands-on work (tailoring, not inventing)
T2: Mentioning the dropped PhD that notes say not to mention
T3: Claiming deep AWS, Java or professional Rust
T4: Inventing a reason for leaving beyond the reorg
T5: Old cover letter is an internal promotion letter to Streamhaus; must not be reused for a new company
T6: Saying he is currently employed at Streamhaus (he left Aug 2026; CV date range ends 2026 (Aug))

# OUTPUT 1: CV
RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Backend Engineer (Python) | Principal Software Engineer
Munich, Germany | rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 | linkedin.com/in/rmk-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer and engineering leader with 21 years of experience building large-scale services in
Python, Go and C++. Experienced in platform architecture, API and distributed-systems development,
event ingestion, and service reliability. Led organisations of up to 45 engineers and defined architecture
for platforms serving more than 50 million users, while continuing to write code regularly, most recently
for internal tooling.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Director of Engineering, Platform | Streamhaus GmbH (video streaming), Munich
2019 – August 2026
• Led a platform organisation of five teams, 45 engineers and five engineering managers, responsible for
identity, playback API, billing integration and developer platform.
• Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services on GKE;
improved playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%.
• Reduced cloud spend by 31% (EUR 4.2M per year) through rightsizing, committed-use discounts and
an internal cost dashboard.
• Introduced an RFC process, architecture review board and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide.
• Grew the organisation from 18 to 45 engineers and conducted more than 200 interviews.
Principal Engineer | Streamhaus GmbH
2015 – 2019
• Served as technical lead for the playback API, using Python, Tornado, an internal framework similar
to FastAPI, Cassandra and Redis.
• Designed an entitlement service handling 120,000 requests per second at peak, using Go and
Cassandra.
• Co-authored the company’s service template and Python style guide.
Senior Software Engineer | Nordfels Telematik AG, Stuttgart
2010 – 2015
• Built backend systems for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300,000 vehicles using C++,
Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
• Led a team of six developers on the route-history product.
Software Engineer | Dataquelle Systems GmbH, Karlsruhe
2005 – 2010
• Developed C++ and Python software for industrial data acquisition on Linux and embedded x86.
• Built a Python test harness used by QA for eight years.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Python (Django, Flask, FastAPI, Tornado, asyncio), Go, C++ (older)
Databases and messaging: PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cassandra, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP (GKE, Pub/Sub, BigQuery), AWS (EC2, S3), Kubernetes,
Terraform
Monitoring and protocols: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, gRPC, Protobuf
Other: Distributed systems design, architecture reviews, technical hiring, people management
EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. (equivalent MSc), Computer Science | Rhine Valley University, 2005
LANGUAGES
German (native), Italian (native), English (fluent)
PUBLICATIONS & TALKS
• “Running Python at 100k rps” – EuroPython-style conference talk, 2018
• “Cost is a feature” – internal platform engineering summit keynote, 2023

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Rafael Moretti-Klein
Munich, Germany|rafael.morettiklein@example.com|+49 555 0505
505|linkedin.com/in/rmk-example
Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) position on Tessel Cargo Software’s Routing &
Tracking team. The role’s focus on reliable event ingestion and tracking-related backend systems
closely matches my experience building high-volume backend systems in Python and Go,
including services that process data from 300,000 vehicles.
At Nordfels Telematik, I built fleet-telematics backend systems using Python, C++,
PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ, ingesting GPS data from 300,000 vehicles. At Streamhaus,
I served as technical lead for the playback API, using Python and designed a Go entitlement
service that handled 120,000 requests per second at peak. As Director of Engineering, I drove the
migration from a Python 2 monolith to around 60 Python and Go services on GKE, improving
playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%. These experiences have given me a strong
foundation in event-driven systems, API reliability and the practical trade-offs involved in scaling
services.
I would bring hands-on Python expertise, experience with PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes,
Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana and OpenTelemetry, as well as a record of improving service
ownership and engineering practices. At Streamhaus, I introduced architecture reviews and
on-call guidelines adopted company-wide; earlier, I built a Python test harness used by QA for
eight years. Tessel’s emphasis on dependable services, clear documentation and service ownership
matches my experience introducing RFCs, architecture reviews, Python service standards and
on-call guidelines.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my backend and platform experience could
contribute to Tessel’s shipment-tracking platform. Thank you for your consideration.
Kind regards,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
